description: March 18 birthday meaning: Pisces decan 3, birthday number 9, Life Path by year, Chinese zodiac note and famous birthdays.
answer: In Western astrology, a March 18 birthday falls in Pisces, in the third decan, with Neptune as the sign's ruler and Pluto as the decan's. In numerology the day gives birthday number 9. The Life Path also uses the birth year. Pisces is mutable and water.

sections.heading: March 18 zodiac sign and personality
paragraphs: On March 18 the Sun reaches roughly twenty-seven degrees of Pisces. Eighteen reduces to 9, the number of endings and compassion, and the late Pisces placement adds a sense of closing chapters. Pluto's decan deepens this. The reading is someone wise beyond their years about letting go, often a gentle presence for others in transition.

On March 18 the Sun usually sits at about 27° Pisces, in the third decan, where Pluto is the sub-ruler alongside Neptune. Pluto, modern ruler of Scorpio, governs the last ten degrees of Pisces, which cover roughly March 11 to March 20. At the very end of the zodiac, the sign's empathy gains depth, focus and a capacity for transformation. Those born here are often described as perceptive, private and drawn to the hidden side of life, whether psychology, mystery or spiritual work. Feelings run strong and sometimes stay unspoken. Pluto adds resilience and a talent for helping others through change. When this decan trusts its intensity rather than hiding it, sensitivity tends to become a genuine strength.

sections.heading: March 18 in numerology
paragraphs: A birthday on the 18th reduces as 1 + 8 = 9, so the birthday number is 9. The compound pairs the 1's leadership with the 8's capacity to organise and manage, then turns both towards the 9's humanitarian outlook. Eighteenth-born people are often described as able to make a real difference: they can organise a fundraiser, run a team or argue a cause convincingly. Emotional openness may sometimes lag behind their practical help. This secondary number tends to suit those who use their influence for others rather than for status, and who measure success by what it changes.

The Life Path, the main number in a numerology chart, also uses the birth year, so it changes from one March 18 birthday to the next: it is 1 for 1960, 2 for 1970, 3 for 1980 and 4 for 1990, for example.

sections.heading: Born on March 18: season, famous birthdays and Chinese zodiac
paragraphs: A March birthday falls around the spring equinox for the northern hemisphere, the season of thaw and first growth, while southern birthdays mark the turn into autumn. The month is split between Pisces and Aries, with the change around March 20 or 21. In numerology March is month 3, linked with expression, creativity and sociability, a lively number for a month that ends with the zodiac starting over. March 18 is the 77th day of the year (78th in a leap year). By March 21, 3 days later, the Sun has usually moved on into Aries.

For the Chinese zodiac, Lunar New Year has always passed by March 18, so the animal is simply the one for the birth year. Well-known people born on March 18 include Grover Cleveland (1837), Neville Chamberlain (1869) and Rudolf Diesel (1858).

faq.question: What zodiac sign is March 18?
faq.answer: March 18 is Pisces in every year from 1930 to 2030, wherever you were born. It falls in the third decan of Pisces, which tradition links with Pluto.

faq.question: What is the Life Path number for someone born on March 18?
faq.answer: It depends on the birth year. On March 18 the Life Path is 1 in 1960, 2 in 1970, 3 in 1980, 4 in 1990, 5 in 2000, 6 in 2010 and 7 in 2020. The birthday number, from the day alone, is 9 for everyone born on the 18th.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac sign is someone born on March 18?
faq.answer: Chinese astrology is straightforward for a March 18 birthday: the new year began weeks earlier, so the birth year's own animal applies.

faq.question: Which famous people were born on March 18?
faq.answer: March 18 is also the birthday of Grover Cleveland (1837), Neville Chamberlain (1869) and Rudolf Diesel (1858). The list comes from Wikidata and favours people with the most Wikipedia articles.
